newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Bank of Cyprus sees 97 results steady.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Cyprus sees 97 results steady.

text.p: The Bank of Cyprus, Cyprus's largest financial institution, on Wednesday forecast 1997 earnings would not show any marked increase over 1996.

"It is expected that the results will be at the same levels as 1996 mainly because of the increase in activities abroad and mainly in Greece," bank chairman Solon Triantafyllides told a news conference.

The Cypriot bank reported operational profits of 46.4 million pounds ($89.8 million) in 1996, up 8.1 percent from the previous year. Eighteen percent of its total is derived from activities of the bank's branches in Greece.
Net earnings rose 5.4 percent to 24.2 million pounds.

Triantafyllides told shareholders the outlook should be considered satisfactory since income derived from commercial activities and tourism are not expected to show any marked increase during the year. And gains from banking activities in Cyprus are expected to be slightly lower, he added.
Shareholders approved a final dividend of 12 percent, in addition to an interim dividend of six percent paid in 1996.
Bank of Cyprus has nine branches in Greece and plans to open another four in future. It expanded to Greece in 1991.
The creation of an investment and securities house offering fund management, corporate finance and financial services is under consideration, Triantafyllides said.

He further revealed the bank is re-examining the possibility of a listing on the Athens stock exchange. The bank previously opted out because of the considerable gap in the PE ratio of listed Greek banks and Cypriot banks. Those differences have now been phased out because of recent highs on the Athens bourse, he said.
It is also planning further expansions in London, home to a large Cypriot community.
"We have already received preliminary approval from the Bank of England for the operation of a sub-branch of the Bank of Cyprus in London which will work parallel to Bank of Cyprus (London)."
The bank, said Triantafyllides, would cater to corporate clients, a facility the Bank of Cyprus (London) is currently not able to handle because of its low capital base.

Last year the Bank of Cyprus embarked on a successful capital raising programme, floating 40 million pounds worth of subordinated convertible bonds denominated in the Cyprus pound to international investors. It is the first Cypriot bank to have done so.
Another 10 million in convertible bonds was floated at home.
The bank plans a 25 million pound rights issue later this month. Both issues will increase the group's capital base to 290 million pounds from an estimated 205 million pounds in 1995.
"With this increase the group enters the year 2000 with a very strong capital base ready to face any challenge from Cyprus's accession to Europe," Triantafyllides said. ($=0.516 pounds)
